subject: chemistry
title: IR Infrared: Bonds That Vibrate
welcome_lead: Identify functional groups from characteristic IR absorptions.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on IR spectroscopy interpretation.
final_note: You can hear the vibrations of bonds in cm^-1.

concepts.def: Absorbs IR to excite bond vibrations.

walkthroughs.body_html:
C-H ~3000 cm^-1. C=O 1680-1750. O-H alcohol 3230-3550 (broad). O-H carboxylic 2500-3300 (very broad).

N-H 3300-3500 (narrow). C-O ester 1000-1300. C=C 1620-1680 (weak/medium).

Broad O-H above 3200 + strong C=O near 1700 = carboxylic acid.

Broad O-H above 3200, no C=O = alcohol. Strong C=O alone = ketone or aldehyde (use NMR/Tollens' to distinguish).

Below 1500 cm^-1 contains overlapping bands unique to each compound.

Match unknown to a database spectrum to identify exact compound. Useful for distinguishing isomers (e.g. propan-1-ol vs propan-2-ol).
